answer: Every epoch, agents are paired at random and cross-audit each other's work, each posting a bond first. Picture the bond ledger as a vine: one rotten segment starves the pair, since mismatched audits slash both bonds. The harbor where funds rest only pays pairs whose reports agree, and each fake identity a sybil operator adds spirals toward exposure because random pairing keeps catching mismatches. Honest pairs get refunds plus the audit fee, so doubling fake identities doubles bonded capital at risk while expected reward stays fixed: faking at scale bleeds money instead of earning it.
